title: Part 2 — HTML & CSS
tagline: From the first HTML tag to a responsive page with a live link.
intro: The longest part in video hours, but the one with the quickest results: change a line of CSS, save, and the page changes.
Finish part 1 first: VS Code, the terminal and Git are used from the first step.

sections.title: Overview
sections.summary: Six steps, about five to six weeks.

blocks.caption: Each step is a skill; the step-4 project uses all the ones before.

items.label: CSS & the box model
items.detail: Pick elements with selectors and change colour, size and spacing
explain: Every element is a box of content, padding, border and margin. box-sizing: border-box makes width include padding and border, far easier to size.
The more specific selector wins: #id beats .class, .class beats a tag. When CSS does not apply, open DevTools and see which line is struck out.

items.label: Flexbox layout
items.detail: Line elements up in rows or columns, centre them, share out space
explain: display: flex on a parent puts its children in a row. justify-content aligns along the row, align-items across it, and gap spaces the children.
The menu, product cards and footer in the Shopee project are all flexbox. The six properties in the table below cover 90% of layouts.

items.label: BEM & projects
items.detail: Name classes by a rule, then build The Band and Shopee with the videos
explain: BEM names classes block__element--modifier: card, card__title, card--featured. A class name tells you which block it belongs to, so CSS rarely clashes.
Follow the video once, then delete a block such as the header and rebuild it without watching. The rebuilding is the learning.

items.label: Responsive
items.detail: One page that fits phones, tablets and desktops
explain: The viewport meta tag makes phones render at their real width. A media query changes CSS above a breakpoint, for example from 768px up.
Test in DevTools: Ctrl + Shift + M (Cmd + Shift + M on a Mac) turns on device mode; pick an iPhone or drag the width.

items.label: GitHub Pages
items.detail: Put the page online for free, with a link to share
explain: Push to GitHub, turn on Pages in Settings, pick the main branch. A minute later the page runs at your-username.github.io/repo-name.
Every push updates GitHub Pages automatically. This is the first link for your portfolio.

sections.title: Your first web page
sections.summary: Ten minutes from an empty folder to a page in the browser.

items: Create a folder and open it in VS Code (the two commands below).
In VS Code create index.html, type ! and press Tab: VS Code fills in an HTML skeleton.
Make it match the sample HTML below, and add a style.css next to it.
Right-click index.html and choose Open with Live Server. The browser opens the page at 127.0.0.1:5500.
Change a colour in style.css and save: the page follows. Commit and push the folder to GitHub as in part 1.

sections.title: Responsive, step by step
sections.summary: Write for phones first, then widen for big screens.

items: Check the viewport meta tag is in the head (VS Code's ! skeleton includes it).
Write CSS for narrow screens first: one column, text big enough to read.
Add a min-width media query for each larger breakpoint, such as 768px for tablets and 1024px for desktops.
Test in DevTools device mode (Ctrl + Shift + M), dragging the width from 320px to 1440px to find what breaks.
Open it on a real phone: on the same Wi-Fi, visit your computer's IP with Live Server's port, such as 192.168.1.5:5500.

blocks.caption: Mobile-first: one column by default, two from 768px, four from 1024px.

body: WSL: Live Server runs inside Ubuntu, so a phone may not reach it by IP. If so, test on the phone after publishing to GitHub Pages.

sections.title: Publish on GitHub Pages
sections.summary: Free, a link right away, and updated on every push.

items: Create a GitHub repo such as my-landing-page and push to it as in part 1. The main file must be called index.html.
On the repo page: Settings → Pages.
Under Build and deployment choose Source: Deploy from a branch, Branch: main, folder / (root), and press Save.
Wait about a minute and reload Settings → Pages: the link your-username.github.io/my-landing-page appears.
Edit, commit, push: the live page updates a few minutes later.
